correctness.rationale: The two nonsingular branches have divided differences equal to ±1 modulo 3, so each contributes one preimage at every level. With w=2t−1 the third branch is 3(w²−1)(9w²−1)/128. Its quadratic coefficient after subtracting 3/128 and factoring 3w² is 1 modulo 3; its Hensel square root b(w) satisfies b(t)−b(s)∈9(t−s)Z_3, making w↦wb(w) bijective on all quotients and on Z_3. This gives the square-root count including the factor of three in the lifts and k=1. The period 3^(k+1) works in each branch, but the shift 3^k fails in the n≡1 branch by its exact isometry. Counting nonzero square residues by even valuation and counting the zero roots give the histogram; the square set has measure (1/3)∑3^(−2j)=3/8, and scaling by three gives 1/8 for the enhancement set, not the full image. Replayed independently by separate branch histograms and the failing period shift for k=1,…,8 (`python3 /workspace/frozen_review_replay.py 3`); this supports but does not replace the all-level proof. The frozen script was read, not run.
